china/early-civilization.4fea711629dd: In Yuanmou, Yunnan, scientists found early humans from about one point seven million years ago: Yuanmou Man, the earliest early humans so far confirmed in China.
china/early-civilization.856eb2fa530c: Memory hint: Bone spade, 骨耜, Hemudu rice fields.
china/early-civilization.3ed13b3215e5: About four thousand to five thousand years ago, the Yan and Yellow Emperor tribes of the Yellow River valley allied, defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu, and gradually formed the Huaxia people. The two are honoured as the first ancestors of Chinese civilization.
china/early-civilization.ae08a11f0834: At Zhoukoudian near Beijing lived Peking Man, about seven hundred thousand to two hundred thousand years ago. They made chipped stone tools, used natural fire and lived in groups.
china/early-civilization.3df96e150acd: Hemudu stilt house. Raised on wooden piles above wet ground. The Hemudu site is in Yuyao, Zhejiang, in the Yangtze River valley, about seven thousand years old. Wooden piles were driven into the ground, beams and floorboards laid on top, then the house built above: a stilt, ganlan-style, house. The south is warm, wet and rainy. A raised floor stays dry, lets air flow, and keeps out snakes and insects.
china/early-civilization.39dbb016706d: Zoom in on the last few thousand years: Hemudu, Banpo, the legendary age of the Yan and Yellow Emperors, then Yao, Shun and Yu, about twenty seventy B C E, Yu founds the Xia dynasty.
china/early-civilization.bfc4b24d74df: Millet field. A drought-tolerant crop for the dry north. Banpo people grew millet, 粟, foxtail millet. China is one of the first countries in the world to grow millet. They farmed with polished stone tools such as stone axes, spades and knives, grew vegetables and raised pigs and dogs.
china/early-civilization.9b86dc8d89a2: In a cave at the top of the same hill lived Upper Cave Man, about thirty thousand years ago. They looked like modern people and sewed clothes with bone needles.
china/early-civilization.76e3cc329f65: Semi-subterranean floor. The floor is dug below ground — warm and windproof. The Banpo site is near Xi’an, Shaanxi, in the Yellow River valley, about six thousand years old. The floor was dug into the ground, so the house was half below and half above the surface: a semi-subterranean house. The north is drier and colder with thick loess soil; digging down saved materials and kept the house warm.
china/early-civilization.4d1340515429: Farming began about ten thousand years ago. Along the Yangtze, Hemudu people grew RICE, about seven thousand years ago; along the Yellow River, Banpo people grew MILLET, about six thousand years ago.

china/division-integration.eddc2902cad0: In three hundred seventeen Sima Rui founded the Eastern Jin at Jiankang, while the north entered the Sixteen Kingdoms period. Large numbers of northerners moved south, bringing labour and advanced farming techniques; with good natural conditions and relative peace, the Jiangnan region was developed.
china/division-integration.f353e0e234d2: Northern Wei later split into Eastern and Western Wei, replaced by Northern Qi and Northern Zhou. In five hundred eighty-one Yang Jian founded the Sui; in five hundred eighty-nine Sui conquered Chen and reunified north and south, ending nearly four centuries of division.
china/division-integration.003500dc809f: Late in the Eastern Han, the Yellow Turban uprising broke out in one hundred eighty-four. Afterwards local strongmen and officials raised their own armies: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao in the north, the Sun family in Jiangdong, Liu Biao in Jing Province and Liu Zhang in Yi Province.
china/division-integration.a7e07067109e: Battle of Chibi, two hundred eight. Around today’s Chibi, Hubei, Sun Quan and Liu Bei versus Cao Cao. In two hundred eight Cao Cao marched south; the allied armies of Sun Quan and Liu Bei attacked his fleet with fire at Chibi on the Yangtze. Cao Cao retreated north; this laid the foundation for the three kingdoms.
china/division-integration.de413b617127: Yizhou, Taiwan. Reached by Wu’s fleet in two hundred thirty. In two hundred thirty Sun Quan sent Wei Wen with over ten thousand men by sea to Yizhou. It strengthened the links between the mainland and Taiwan.
china/division-integration.d45df3995189: The Northern Wei, founded by the Tuoba branch of the Xianbei, unified the Yellow River valley in four hundred thirty-nine. In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang and carried out reforms to adopt Han culture, promoting the blending of the northern peoples.
china/division-integration.04cf07081065: Each kingdom developed: Wei built irrigation and military farms, and the northern economy recovered; Zhuge Liang governed Shu and developed the southwest; in two hundred thirty Wu sent Wei Wen with a fleet to Yizhou, today’s Taiwan, strengthening links between the mainland and Taiwan.
china/division-integration.fab5688d590a: In three hundred eighty-three, at the Battle of the Fei River, the Eastern Jin defeated Former Qin, which had unified the north, with far fewer troops. From four hundred twenty the south was ruled in turn by the Song, Qi, Liang and Chen — the Southern Dynasties — all from Jiankang.
china/division-integration.1b054a5850bc: Wei. In two hundred twenty Cao Pi became emperor; capital Luoyang. Wei built irrigation works and military farms, tuntian; the northern economy recovered. Wei conquered Shu in two hundred sixty-three.
china/division-integration.73b83d0637cf: Shu, Han. In two hundred twenty-one Liu Bei became emperor in Chengdu; the state is called Shu. Zhuge Liang governed well and helped develop the southwest.
china/division-integration.ad734287abba: In two hundred Cao Cao met Yuan Shao at Guandu. Though outnumbered, Cao Cao raided Wuchao and burned Yuan’s grain — a victory of the few over the many. Afterwards Cao Cao gradually unified the north.
china/division-integration.1cc6070a3dcc: Wei conquered Shu in two hundred sixty-three; in two hundred sixty-six Sima Yan founded the Western Jin at Luoyang, and in two hundred eighty it conquered Wu, ending the division. Meanwhile the Xiongnu, Xianbei, Jie, Di and Qiang moved inward in large numbers and lived among the Han. After the War of the Eight Princes, the Western Jin fell in three hundred sixteen.
china/division-integration.57c3f34cda18: Jianye or Jiankang, Nanjing. Capital of Wu, Eastern Jin and the Southern Dynasties. Wu’s capital Jianye was renamed Jiankang in the Jin. Eastern Jin and all four Southern Dynasties, Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, ruled from here; it became a great commercial city.
china/division-integration.31f3f69f2281: Battle of Guandu, two hundred. Near today’s Zhongmou, Henan, Cao Cao versus Yuan Shao. Cao Cao, with a smaller army, burned Yuan Shao’s grain stores at Wuchao and won. A famous victory of the few over the many; it laid the foundation for Cao Cao to unify the north.
china/division-integration.2e3e5fdd59ba: Wu. In two hundred twenty-two Sun Quan became King of Wu; capital later Jianye, today’s Nanjing. In two hundred thirty Wu sent Wei Wen with a fleet to Yizhou, today’s Taiwan. The economy of the Jiangnan region began to develop.
china/division-integration.86cc6b30736e: In two hundred twenty Cao Pi became emperor of Wei with its capital at Luoyang. The next year Liu Bei became emperor in Chengdu, the state is called Shu. In two hundred twenty-two Sun Quan became King of Wu, later with its capital at Jianye. The three kingdoms stood like the three legs of a ding.
china/division-integration.12963c0ba386: Chengdu. Capital of Shu. Liu Bei became emperor here in two hundred twenty-one. Zhuge Liang governed Shu and developed the southwest.
china/division-integration.05a62a780496: In two hundred eight Cao Cao marched south with a great army. Sun Quan and Liu Bei joined forces and used fire to destroy his fleet at Chibi on the Yangtze. Cao Cao retreated north. The battle laid the foundation for the three kingdoms.

china/chinese-spirit.fc8d12da6fa9: Nineteen sixty-four. Yuan Longping. Yuan finds a male-sterile rice plant.
china/chinese-spirit.a6b8c360e1a0: Nineteen seventy-one. Tu Youyou. A sweet wormwood extract works against malaria parasites in an animal test.
china/chinese-spirit.0be52e54e541: Nineteen seventy-two. Tu Youyou. Tu’s team isolates the compound later named artemisinin.
china/chinese-spirit.04cda3fb6982: Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu grew up in China and worked as a physicist in the U.S. She and her collaborators showed that one kind of radioactive decay behaves differently from its mirror image. They cooled cobalt sixty and used a magnetic field to line up its nuclear spins. More electrons came out in the direction opposite to the spins.
china/chinese-spirit.5bc875302d28: Tu Youyou. Tu led a team that discovered artemisinin, a compound used to treat malaria. She received half of the twenty fifteen Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. A fourth-century medical text by Ge Hong described soaking sweet wormwood. That gave Tu’s team an idea: try extracting substances from the plant at a lower temperature.
china/chinese-spirit.ee8dd4c61dfe: Nineteen fifty-seven. Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu and her collaborators publish their experimental results.
china/chinese-spirit.8ad0a6d139cf: Nineteen sixty. Red Flag Canal workers. Work begins on the Red Flag Canal in Lin County.
china/chinese-spirit.47a11bab4e6c: Yuan Longping. Yuan and other researchers bred high-yield hybrid rice by crossing different lines of rice. In nineteen sixty-four, he examined clusters of rice flowers with a magnifying glass. He found a male-sterile plant. It made no pollen that could fertilize an egg, but pollen from another line could help it set seed.
china/chinese-spirit.42a15f79dc54: Twenty fifteen. Tu Youyou. Tu shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
china/chinese-spirit.e5e7ac5e05f5: Nineteen sixty-nine. Red Flag Canal workers. The full Red Flag Canal network, including its branch channels, is completed.
china/chinese-spirit.e2781c3bcfc1: Qian Xuesen. Qian worked with Caltech’s early rocketry team and later helped build China’s rocket and space programs. U.S. authorities barred him from leaving for several years. Once the ban was lifted in nineteen fifty-five, he and his family left Los Angeles by ship for China.
china/chinese-spirit.c023bfa65609: Nineteen sixty-five. Red Flag Canal workers. Water begins flowing through the Red Flag Canal’s main channel.
china/chinese-spirit.24348324c1f5: Zhan Tianyou. Zhan led construction of the railway from Beijing to Zhangjiakou. It opened in nineteen oh nine. At Qinglongqiao, he laid out a switchback. Trains could take a longer route up the mountain by reversing direction on the tracks.
china/chinese-spirit.ca51d520fca2: Nineteen fifty-eight. Deng Jiaxian. Deng takes on classified research.
china/chinese-spirit.1440f9ef8e5d: Deng Jiaxian. Deng led teams in China’s early nuclear weapons program. Yang Zhenning later wrote about him in the essay “Deng Jiaxian.” In nineteen fifty-eight he took on classified work. He could no longer tell even his family where he was going for work.
china/chinese-spirit.456036058abb: Nineteen fifty-five. Qian Xuesen. After the U.S. travel ban is lifted, Qian returns to China.
china/chinese-spirit.acf377ba63a7: Nineteen thirty. Wen Yiduo. Wen takes a teaching post in Qingdao, where he studies Tang poetry.
china/chinese-spirit.6215996c0488: Nineteen oh nine. Zhan Tianyou. The Beijing-Zhangjiakou Railway opens.
china/chinese-spirit.4a6729b7aa12: Nineteen twenty-nine. Lin Qiaozhi. Lin graduates and joins the staff at Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
china/chinese-spirit.fceafdeabd25: Lin Qiaozhi. Lin cared for mothers and newborns and helped develop medical care for women in China. In the nineteen fifties, she sent staff to the Soviet Union to learn how to examine cells for signs of disease. After they returned, her team began screening for cervical cancer.

china/dynasties.eec027915aa4: Republic of China, nineteen twelve to nineteen forty-nine. Nineteen twelve to nineteen forty-nine. Nineteen twelve: no more emperors. On the first of January, nineteen twelve, the Republic of China was founded in Nanjing, with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president. The nineteen eleven Revolution, 辛亥革命, overthrew Qing and ended over two thousand years of rule by emperors. The period was full of struggle: warlords, the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, nineteen thirty-one to nineteen forty-five, and civil war.
china/dynasties.c8bd1a0de1d0: Xia. Circa twenty seventy to sixteen hundred B C E. Father to son: the first hereditary throne. When Yu’s son Qi inherited the throne, “all under heaven” became one family’s business. That rule — the throne stays in the family — lasted four thousand years. Around twenty seventy B C E Yu founded Xia — the textbook’s first dynasty. Before Xia, leaders were chosen by merit, “abdication”, 禅让. After Yu, his son Qi took the throne, and power stayed in the family.
china/dynasties.6b8f96bd5c5e: Northern Song, Liao, Western Xia. Northern Song nine hundred sixty to eleven twenty-seven. The Chanyuan Treaty, ten oh five. After a war, Song and Liao made peace: Song paid silver and silk each year, and the two sides traded peacefully for over one hundred years. Bi Sheng, 毕昇, invented movable-type printing. In Sichuan, merchants began using jiaozi, 交子, the world’s earliest paper money.
china/dynasties.d2f92d4f8fd5: Yuan. Twelve seventy-one to thirteen sixty-eight. The province system, 行省制度. Yuan divided its huge empire into provinces, 行省. It was the start of China’s province system — the “provinces” on today’s map come from it. Kublai Khan named his dynasty Yuan in twelve seventy-one. Yuan took Lin’an in twelve seventy-six and finished off the last Song resistance in twelve seventy-nine. The Xuanzheng Yuan, 宣政院, governed Tibet; a Penghu inspectorate, 澎湖巡检司, managed Penghu and Liuqiu, today’s Taiwan.
china/dynasties.502f3f419076: Eastern Jin and Sixteen Kingdoms. Eastern Jin three hundred seventeen to four hundred twenty. Battle of the Fei River, three hundred eighty-three. Former Qin, 前秦, which had united the north, attacked with a huge army. The smaller Eastern Jin army won — and gave Chinese the idiom “every tree and blade of grass looks like a soldier”, 草木皆兵. In the north many regimes rose and fell — the “Sixteen Kingdoms”, 十六国. Huge numbers of northerners moved south, bringing farming skills; the Jiangnan region, south of the Yangtze, began to boom.
china/dynasties.7019fddc76ad: Three Kingdoms. Two hundred twenty to two hundred eighty. After Red Cliffs: a three-way split. In two hundred eight Sun Quan and Liu Bei together beat Cao Cao’s bigger army at Red Cliffs, 赤壁 — with fire ships and smart use of wind and river. It set up the three-way split. Wei was founded in two hundred twenty, Shu in two hundred twenty-one, Wu in two hundred twenty-two — “three legs of a cauldron”, 三国鼎立. Zhuge Liang, 诸葛亮, ran Shu. In two hundred thirty Wu’s ruler Sun Quan sent a fleet to Yizhou, today’s Taiwan; 夷洲.
china/dynasties.caa48fedcfbc: Memory hook Dynasty Song: 宋元明清后, 皇朝至此完.
china/dynasties.8d58d3a8f4ba: Zhongdu. Today: Southwest Beijing. The Jin moved their capital to Zhongdu in eleven fifty-three. This was the first time a dynasty made the Beijing area its main capital.
china/dynasties.2ce88da7b823: Western Zhou. Ten forty-six to seven hundred seventy-one B C E. The enfeoffment system, 分封制. The Zhou king gave land and people to relatives and heroes, making them lords, 诸侯, who guarded the realm and sent tribute — a bit like medieval Europe’s lords and vassals. In ten forty-six B C E King Wu beat the Shang army at the Battle of Muye, 牧野之战. In seven hundred seventy-one B C E the Quanrong, 犬戎, captured Haojing and Western Zhou ended.
china/dynasties.8cf3c199abec: Western Han. Two hundred two B C E to eight C E. Zhang Qian opens the Silk Road. In one hundred thirty-eight B C E Zhang Qian, 张骞, set off west — and was captured for over ten years before getting home. His trips opened the Silk Road, linking Chang’an to Central Asia and on towards Rome. Emperor Wu, 汉武帝, made Han strongest and made Confucianism the official teaching, 罢黜百家, 尊崇儒术. In sixty B C E Han set up the Protector-General of the Western Regions, 西域都护 — today’s Xinjiang came under the central government from then on.
china/dynasties.4cdc9f02a3e7: Tang. Six hundred eighteen to nine hundred seven. A golden age: Chang’an, world city. Under Emperor Taizong, the “Zhenguan reign”, and Emperor Xuanzong, the “Kaiyuan golden age”, Chang’an held about a million people — merchants, monks and students from across Asia. Six hundred forty-one: Princess Wencheng, 文成公主, travelled to Tibet to marry the Tubo king Songtsen Gampo, 松赞干布. Seven hundred fifty-five: the An-Shi Rebellion, 安史之乱, began — the turning point from glory to decline.
china/dynasties.d10b031caa58: People’s Republic of China, nineteen forty-nine onward. Nineteen forty-nine to today. Nineteen forty-nine: New China. The founding of the PRC opened a new era in Chinese history. On the first of October, nineteen forty-nine, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China in Tiananmen Square. At seventy-seven years old, the PRC is younger than the USA, two hundred fifty.
china/dynasties.b439d19d3ed6: Ming. Thirteen sixty-eight to sixteen forty-four. Zheng He sails seven times, fourteen oh five to fourteen thirty-three. Admiral Zheng He, 郑和, led fleets of up to two hundred plus ships as far as East Africa — decades before Columbus. Emperor Yongle moved the capital to Beijing in fourteen twenty-one and built the Forbidden City. Ming rebuilt the Great Wall in brick and stone, from the Yalu River to Jiayu Pass.
china/dynasties.a5f1d6e7b260: Eastern Zhou. Seven hundred seventy to two hundred fifty-six B C E, Spring and Autumn seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six, Warring States four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one. Seven states, a hundred schools of thought. War pushed change: iron tools, new laws, and thinkers like Confucius, Mozi, Laozi and Han Fei arguing about how to run a country — the “Hundred Schools of Thought”. Spring and Autumn, seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six B C E: strong lords competed to be “hegemon”. Confucius, 孔子, taught. Warring States, four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one B C E: seven big states. Shang Yang’s reforms, 商鞅变法, made Qin the strongest; Li Bing, 李冰, built the Dujiangyan irrigation system.
china/dynasties.6c4351b808d2: Memory hook Dynasty Song: 三分魏蜀吴, 二晋前后延;
china/dynasties.29d758953e7c: Memory hook Dynasty Song: 南北朝并立, 隋唐五代传;
china/dynasties.0ed0b29b6fb5: Wulei, Protectorate of the Western Regions. Today: east of Luntai, Xinjiang. Setting up the Protectorate here in sixty B C E marked the Western Regions, today’s Xinjiang, officially becoming part of China’s territory.
china/dynasties.71f1bd5b64e0: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms. Nine hundred seven to nine hundred sixty, Five Dynasties. Five dynasties in fifty-three years. The north changed hands five times while about ten smaller kingdoms ruled the south. The south saw less war, so its farms and towns kept growing. In the north, Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han and Later Zhou followed one another in just fifty-three years. Nine hundred sixteen: the Khitan, 契丹, leader Abaoji founded the state later called Liao; in nine hundred thirty-eight it gained the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan-Yun, including today’s Beijing.
china/dynasties.769194e58e71: Memory hook Dynasty Song: 春秋和战国, 一统秦两汉;
china/dynasties.3b6d7fde473a: Western Jin. Two hundred sixty-six to three hundred sixteen. Two hundred eighty: China reunited — for a while. Jin conquered Wu in two hundred eighty and ended sixty years of division. It lasted about thirty-five years before the north broke apart again. In two hundred sixty-six Sima Yan took the throne from Wei and founded Jin. The unity was short: princes fought each other, rebellions broke out, and Western Jin fell in three hundred sixteen.
china/dynasties.07ab9ded8fa0: Southern Song, Jin. Southern Song eleven twenty-seven to twelve seventy-nine. Yue Fei fights Jin; the economy moves south. General Yue Fei, 岳飞, won big victories against Jin. Meanwhile the south grew richer than the north — by Southern Song, China’s economic centre had moved south for good. Eleven forty-two: Song and Jin made peace, with a border along the Huai River and Dasan Pass, 大散关. “When Suzhou and Huzhou have a good harvest, the whole country has enough”, 苏湖熟, 天下足.
china/dynasties.7fd25a9e66af: Sui. Five hundred eighty-one to six hundred eighteen. The Grand Canal and the imperial exams. Sui dug the Grand Canal to move grain from the rich south to the north, and began choosing officials by exam instead of by family — the imperial examinations, 科举. Five hundred eighty-nine: Sui conquered Chen and reunited China after almost three hundred years of division. The Grand Canal ran two thousand plus kilometers, one thousand two hundred forty plus miles, from Zhuojun, today’s Beijing, to Yuhang, today’s Hangzhou, centred on Luoyang — about New York to Miami.
china/dynasties.da3cf036bfa7: Northern and Southern Dynasties. Four hundred twenty to five hundred eighty-nine. Emperor Xiaowen’s reforms. In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei, a Xianbei 鲜卑 ruler, moved his capital to Luoyang and had his court adopt Han clothes, language and surnames — a big step in the blending of peoples. The south had four dynasties in a row — Song, Qi, Liang, Chen — all ruling from Jiankang. Zu Chongzhi, 祖冲之, calculated pi to between three point one four one five nine two six and three point one four one five nine two seven — the world’s best for about one thousand years.
china/dynasties.b6146ad314ec: Don’t mix up: Eastern Zhou ended in two hundred fifty-six B C E, Qin conquered it, but the Warring States period runs to two hundred twenty-one B C E, when Qin unified China.
china/dynasties.b181cb92da14: Eastern Han. Twenty-five to two hundred twenty. Cai Lun improves paper, one hundred five C E. Cai Lun, 蔡伦, made paper from bark, hemp, rags and old fishing nets — cheap and light. Paper became one of China’s Four Great Inventions. Zhang Heng, 张衡, built a seismoscope, 地动仪, that showed the direction of distant earthquakes. Ban Chao, 班超, restored Han control in the Western Regions; Buddhism arrived from India.
china/dynasties.6713ef2d2a6f: Qin. Two hundred twenty-one to two hundred seven B C E. Two hundred twenty-one B C E: China is unified. Qin conquered the other six states in ten years and created China’s first unified, centralised state ruled by an emperor. Qin itself lasted only fifteen years — but its systems lasted two thousand. He called himself the “First Emperor”, 始皇帝, and ran the country through commanderies and counties, 郡县制, led by officials he appointed. One script, small seal 小篆, one round coin with a square hole, one set of weights and measures — and the Great Wall joined up.
china/dynasties.d60c3e2d3a2f: Memory hook Dynasty Song: 夏商与西周, 东周分两段;
china/dynasties.7fc59db76aac: Shang. Circa sixteen hundred to ten forty-six B C E. Pan Geng moves the capital to Yin. Around thirteen hundred B C E King Pan Geng moved the capital to Yin. Shang settled down there for the rest of the dynasty — and Yin’s ruins, 殷墟, later gave up thousands of oracle bones. Shang kings asked their ancestors questions by cracking turtle shells and ox bones. The answers were carved on them: oracle-bone script, 甲骨文, the oldest mature Chinese writing. The Houmuwu ding, 后母戊鼎, weighs eight hundred thirty-two point eight four kilograms, one thousand eight hundred thirty-six pounds — more than a grand piano. It is the heaviest ancient bronze vessel found in China.
china/dynasties.c2ebc1257f5e: Qing. Sixteen forty-four to nineteen twelve, name Qing from sixteen thirty-six. Kangxi: Taiwan and the Russian border. In sixteen eighty-three Qing brought Taiwan under its rule and in sixteen eighty-four set up Taiwan Prefecture. In sixteen eighty-nine the Treaty of Nerchinsk, 尼布楚条约, with Russia set the northeast border. Emperor Qianlong put down revolts in Xinjiang in the seventeen fifties and secured Qing rule there. Eighteen forty: the Opium War — the start of modern Chinese history. Nineteen twelve: the last emperor abdicated.
china/dynasties.991fb41152a4: Pingcheng. Today: Datong, Shanxi. The Northern Wei ruled the north from Pingcheng. In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital south to Luoyang to be closer to the Central Plains.
china/dynasties.e7df7fe8aae9: Don’t mix up: Qing didn’t start in sixteen forty-four: Hong Taiji renamed his state Qing in sixteen thirty-six; in sixteen forty-four Qing armies entered Beijing.

china/great-wall.d7199941020d: The walkway on top. A road for soldiers along the mountains. At Badaling the top is about five point eight meters, nineteen feet, wide — room for five horses or ten soldiers side by side. Soldiers could move quickly along the wall to wherever the attack came.
china/great-wall.d13ac81d5685: Hollow watchtower, 空心敌台. A fort astride the wall. General Qi Jiguang, 戚继光, famous for fighting pirates, had over a thousand hollow towers built on the wall near Beijing. Soldiers lived and stored weapons inside, and shot along the wall from the windows — crossfire against ladders.

china/ancient-engineering.531058e92115: Column and lintel. Already in place: the red column and the beam along its top. Palace columns are huge single tree trunks, painted red. They stand on stone bases, 柱础, instead of being buried in the ground.
china/ancient-engineering.476581ea9237: Mortise and tenon. Through tenon. A square peg pushed right through a hole in the column. Through tenon. Dovetail. Slide “Assemble” to push the beam’s tenon, 榫, into the column’s mortise, 卯. The joint holds by shape and friction, no nails, no glue. In a quake it can turn a little and rub, soaking up energy, then settle back.

china/ancient-science.fa14082e30b7: Zhang Heng built the seismoscope in one hundred thirty-two, in the Eastern Han. When an earthquake happened, the dragon facing that direction dropped its bronze ball into a toad’s mouth. It detected quakes; it could not predict them.

china/china-space.2a08955a980c: Memory hook: Five carried one: Shenzhou five, Yang Liwei, two thousand three.
china/china-space.ef385bc75d9b: Don’t mix up: Shenzhou one was uncrewed. The first crewed Shenzhou was number five.
china/china-space.4493c51167ac: Don’t mix up: Chang’e three landed on the near side, which faces Earth. The far side came next, with Chang’e four.
china/china-space.6214bbf54933: Don’t mix up: Chang’e five did not carry astronauts. Robots collected the samples.
china/china-space.53914f91f44b: Twenty twenty-two. The Tiangong space station is complete. Three modules — Tianhe, twenty twenty-one, Wentian, July twenty twenty-two, and Mengtian, October twenty twenty-two — joined in a T shape about four hundred kilometers, two hundred fifty miles, up. In November twenty twenty-two two crews, six astronauts, met in orbit for the first time.
china/china-space.48a98526f50f: Don’t mix up: Dongfanghong one carried no people. China’s first astronaut flew thirty-three years later, in two thousand three.
china/china-space.d4bb3a4629aa: Memory hook: Orbit, land, return — 绕, 落, 回.
china/china-space.eb332f206bb2: Two thousand three. Shenzhou five: Yang Liwei, China’s first astronaut. Yang Liwei, 杨利伟, circled Earth fourteen times in about twenty-one hours. China became the third country — after the USSR and the USA — to send a person into space on its own rocket.
china/china-space.8198af0d5622: Twenty thirteen. Chang’e three lands; the Yutu rover rolls off. Chang’e three made the first soft landing on the Moon by any country since nineteen seventy-six, in the Bay of Rainbows region on the near side. It released Yutu, 玉兔, the “Jade Rabbit” who lives with Chang’e in the legend.
china/china-space.3d213d293d16: Twenty twenty-five. Tianwen two heads for an asteroid. On the twenty-ninth of May, twenty twenty-five, a Long March three B launched Tianwen two to collect samples from a small near-Earth asteroid, Kamoʻoalewa. That year China launched about ninety-two rockets — a record. Next goal: Chinese astronauts on the Moon before twenty thirty.
china/china-space.f425f2b535ab: Two thousand seven. Chang’e one orbits the Moon. The lunar programme is named after Chang’e, 嫦娥, the Moon goddess of Chinese legend. Its plan has three steps: orbit, 绕, land, 落, return, 回. Chang’e one did step one and mapped the whole Moon.
china/china-space.b623f9b499b2: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. Today: Ejin Banner, Inner Mongolia, in the desert. China’s first satellite went up from here in nineteen seventy, playing the song “The East Is Red”, and Yang Liwei flew to space from here in two thousand three.
china/china-space.d932f0b5989f: Nineteen ninety-nine. Shenzhou one: a test flight with no crew. China’s crewed spaceflight programme, started in nineteen ninety-two, flew its first spacecraft. Shenzhou, 神舟, means “divine vessel”. Four uncrewed test flights came before anyone climbed aboard.
china/china-space.0408752007b4: Twenty twenty. Chang’e five brings the Moon home. The giant Long March five sent Chang’e five from Wenchang on Hainan Island. It landed in the Ocean of Storms, drilled and scooped one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams, three point eight pounds, of rock and soil, launched back into lunar orbit, and returned to Earth on the seventeenth of December — completing “orbit, land, return”.
china/china-space.fea499163320: Twenty twenty-one. Tianwen one lands the Zhurong rover on Mars. Tianwen one, 天问, “Questions to Heaven”, after an ancient poem, did three jobs on its first try: orbit Mars, land, and drive a rover. Zhurong, 祝融, is named after the god of fire. China became the second country to drive a rover on Mars, after the USA.
china/china-space.99a424c71a94: Don’t mix up: Chang’e is a robot programme. No Chinese astronaut has walked on the Moon yet; that goal is set for before twenty thirty.
china/china-space.8330be9dbfb8: Nineteen seventy. Dongfanghong one: China’s first satellite. A Long March one rocket lifted the one hundred seventy-three kilogram, three hundred eighty pound, satellite from Jiuquan in the Gobi Desert. From orbit it played the song “The East Is Red”, 东方红, back to Earth. China became the fifth country to launch its own satellite.
china/china-space.83467910a458: Memory hook: Five went and came back: one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams.
china/china-space.190327abf1bc: Twenty twelve. Shenzhou nine: the first hand-flown docking. In twenty eleven China launched a small space lab, Tiangong one, 天宫, “Heavenly Palace”, and the uncrewed Shenzhou eight docked with it automatically. In June twenty twelve astronaut Liu Wang flew Shenzhou nine in by hand. On board was Liu Yang, China’s first woman in space.
china/china-space.3547a4e0d288: Two thousand eight. Shenzhou seven: China’s first spacewalk. Zhai Zhigang, 翟志刚, opened the hatch and stepped out into space, waving a Chinese flag. He wore a spacesuit made in China called Feitian, 飞天, “flying to the heavens”.
china/china-space.8f61a3f30cde: Twenty twenty-four. Chang’e six: samples from the far side. Relaying through the new Queqiao two satellite, Chang’e six landed in Apollo crater on the far side, collected one thousand nine hundred thirty-five point three grams of samples, and came home on the twenty-fifth of June — the first far-side samples in history.
china/china-space.03d9176a2850: Don’t mix up: Tiangong one was a small test lab, not the big Tiangong space station of twenty twenty-two.
china/china-space.b63fe82444b7: Don’t mix up: Chang’e five samples are from the near side; Chang’e six samples are from the far side.
china/china-space.06248eb0c510: Don’t mix up: Shenzhou seven was the spacewalk mission; docking came later, with Shenzhou eight and nine.
china/china-space.2696e6ede982: Twenty nineteen. Chang’e four: first-ever landing on the far side. Nobody had ever landed on the far side, because you can’t radio Earth from there. First China parked the Queqiao relay satellite beyond the Moon, May twenty eighteen. Then Chang’e four landed in Von Kármán crater and sent out the Yutu two rover.
china/china-space.8b538725ab3e: Memory hook: Nineteen seventy: the East is Red — and so is the sky.
china/china-space.88d193c46b0e: Don’t mix up: Third country to fly people into space — not the first. And Shenzhou five did not go to the Moon.

china/disasters.9196b34b47c0: Ürümqi. The city farthest from any ocean in the world — about two thousand five hundred kilometers.

china/beijing-capital.fc342b33f7a3: Wanning Bridge. The oldest bridge on the axis, twelve eighty-five. First built in twelve eighty-five in the Yuan dynasty, and still used by traffic today. In Yuan times, grain boats on the Grand Canal passed under it into Jishuitan lake, today’s Shichahai, the canal’s northern end. Stone water creatures carved on its banks once watched the water level.
china/beijing-capital.dd8afaf75939: Tian’anmen. Gate of Heavenly Peace. Built in fourteen seventeen as the front gate of the Imperial City, and given the name Tian’anmen in sixteen fifty-one. On October first, nineteen forty-nine, the founding ceremony of the People’s Republic of China was held here. It appears on China’s national emblem.
china/beijing-capital.f79dd742765a: Festooned gate, 垂花门. The “second gate”. A beautifully carved gate between the front yard and the inner courtyard; its painted wooden “flower” pendants hang down from the eaves. A saying about well-brought-up daughters: “never out the main gate, never past the second gate”, 大门不出, 二门不迈.
china/beijing-capital.d171a9e33ea3: East wing, 东厢房. Faces west. Bedrooms for the younger generation; traditionally the eldest son’s family lived in the east wing. It gets the afternoon sun.
china/beijing-capital.c0f6fd48dc5d: Main gate, 大门. In the southeast corner. The gate is in a corner, not in the middle. Combined with the screen wall right inside, people in the hutong cannot look straight into the yard. It also cuts down the street wind and dust blowing in.
china/beijing-capital.1cd238df1077: Screen wall, 影壁. Blocks the view from the gate. A decorated wall just inside, or opposite, the gate. Visitors turn left into the front yard, so the inside stays private and calm.
china/beijing-capital.c28493b2176f: The Forbidden City, Palace Museum. Home of twenty-four Ming and Qing emperors. Built fourteen oh six to fourteen twenty. About nine hundred sixty-one meters long and seven hundred fifty-three meters wide, about seventy-two hectares, about one hundred thirty-five football fields, ringed by a ten-meter wall and a wide moat. About eight thousand seven hundred rooms, counted in 间, the space between four pillars. The Hall of Supreme Harmony on the axis is China’s largest surviving wooden hall. You go in through the Meridian Gate, 午门, in the south and out through the Gate of Divine Prowess, 神武门, in the north. It became the Palace Museum in nineteen twenty-five and a World Heritage Site in nineteen eighty-seven.
china/beijing-capital.097cb645600e: Zhengyangmen, Qianmen. Main south gate of the inner city. Built in fourteen nineteen. Its gate tower is about forty-three meters, one hundred forty-one feet, tall, the tallest of old Beijing’s city gates. In front stands an arrow tower with rows of small windows, built for archers to defend the gate. Outside it, Qianmen Street has been a busy shopping street for centuries.
china/beijing-capital.afebdd5fa7a9: Main hall, 正房. North side, facing south. The biggest, tallest building, for the grandparents or the head of the family. It faces south, so the low winter sun shines deep inside, while its wide eaves block the high summer sun. Its solid back wall faces north, into the cold winter wind.
china/beijing-capital.320c18ab04e4: Temple of Heaven. Where emperors prayed for good harvests. Built in fourteen twenty for the Ming and Qing emperors to worship heaven and pray for good harvests. World Heritage Site since nineteen ninety-eight. The round Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests has three blue roofs: blue for the sky. It is about thirty-eight meters, one hundred twenty-five feet, tall. The park wall is round in the north and square in the south: “round heaven, square earth”, 天圆地方.
china/beijing-capital.fc3666489c23: Side rooms, 耳房. Small rooms beside the main hall. Lower and smaller, like “ears” on either side of the main hall. Used for storage, a kitchen or a study.
china/beijing-capital.146b93d1d0d6: Jingshan. A man-made hill with the best view. Piled up in the Ming dynasty, largely from the earth dug out for the palace moat. About forty-five meters, one hundred fifty feet, high. The Wanchun Pavilion on top sits exactly on the axis. From the top you can see the golden roofs of the Forbidden City to the south and the Drum Tower to the north.
china/beijing-capital.a64020f0294f: Monument to the People’s Heroes. Today: Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. A thirty-eight-meter granite obelisk on the Central Axis, honouring the people who gave their lives for China’s independence and liberation.
china/beijing-capital.d551a8e02b92: Xiannongtan, Altar of Agriculture. West of the axis. Built in fourteen twenty. Each spring the emperor came here to plough a small field himself, to show how important farming was. It sits to the west of the axis, balancing the Temple of Heaven to the east. Today it houses the Beijing Ancient Architecture Museum.
china/beijing-capital.63ebca0431da: Drum Tower. Telling the time at night. First built in twelve seventy-two, Yuan, rebuilt in the Ming dynasty. About forty-seven meters, one hundred fifty-four feet, tall. Drums were beaten to mark the hours of the night: “morning bell, evening drum”, 晨钟暮鼓. It once held twenty-five drums: one huge drum and twenty-four smaller ones, one for each of the twenty-four solar terms.
china/beijing-capital.dcff64a1131c: Summer Palace. Today: Haidian, Beijing. A huge royal garden with Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake. Its Long Corridor is painted with more than fourteen thousand pictures.
china/beijing-capital.7bf47835757b: West wing, 西厢房. Faces east. More bedrooms for the younger generation. It gets the morning sun.
china/beijing-capital.d9a3f9e97b28: Courtyard, 院子. The family’s outdoor living room. All the rooms open onto the yard, not onto the street: quiet, safe and sunny. Families planted trees such as jujube and crabapple, raised goldfish and sat out on summer evenings.
china/beijing-capital.c04551375674: South row, 倒座房. Faces north, toward the yard. Its back wall is on the hutong, and its windows face north into the front yard. It gets the least sun, so it was used for guests, servants, storage or a study.
china/beijing-capital.72f74863cb15: Olympic Park. The “Bird’s Nest” stadium and the “Water Cube” stand on either side of the Central Axis. Beijing is the first city to host both Summer, two thousand eight, and Winter, twenty twenty-two, Olympics.
china/beijing-capital.3c4a6abd57d3: Great Hall of the People. Today: West side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. The National People’s Congress meets here. Its main auditorium seats about ten thousand people.
china/beijing-capital.55ec19dfc0bf: Drum Tower and Bell Tower. Drums sounded the hours at night and the bell rang at dawn. The bronze bell in the Bell Tower weighs about sixty-three tonnes.
china/beijing-capital.77172be2216e: Bell Tower. The northern end of the axis. Rebuilt in seventeen forty-five to seventeen forty-seven, Qing, entirely of brick and stone, so it could not burn down again. About forty-eight meters, one hundred fifty-seven feet, tall. Its bronze bell, cast in the Ming Yongle years, weighs about sixty-three tonnes: as much as five school buses. You have walked about seven point eight kilometers, about four point eight miles!
china/beijing-capital.dea48e02542c: Tian’anmen Square. One of the largest city squares in the world. About forty-four hectares: roughly eighty US football fields. A national flag-raising ceremony is held here at sunrise every day. On the axis: the Monument to the People’s Heroes, completed nineteen fifty-eight. On the sides: the Great Hall of the People, west, where the National People’s Congress meets, and the National Museum of China, east.
china/beijing-capital.80e815e33ea3: Zhengyangmen, Qianmen. At about forty-three meters, it was the tallest gate of old Beijing. In front stands an arrow tower with rows of little windows for archers.
china/beijing-capital.278b38aaef10: Hutong, 胡同. The lane outside. Old Beijing’s lanes. Most of them run east-west, so the courtyard houses between them can all face south. Many hutongs date back to the Yuan dynasty; one popular theory says the word comes from a Mongolian word for “well”.
china/beijing-capital.009266573f22: Yongdingmen Gate. The southern start of the axis. Built in fifteen fifty-three, Ming dynasty, as the main south gate of the new outer city. The name means “Gate of Lasting Peace”. Torn down in nineteen fifty-seven to make room for traffic, then rebuilt in two thousand four from old drawings and photos. From here the axis runs dead straight north for about seven point eight kilometers, four point eight miles.

yuwen/yw-expository.dcff64a1131c: Summer Palace. Today: Haidian, Beijing. A huge royal garden with Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake. Its Long Corridor is painted with more than fourteen thousand pictures.

art/art-color.9ab940d3478f: Tertiary colors. A primary and its neighbouring secondary: red-orange, blue-green… There are six: red-orange, yellow-orange, yellow-green, blue-green, blue-violet, red-violet. Primary name goes first in English: “blue-green”, not “green-blue”. Three plus three plus six equals the twelve colors of the wheel. Three primaries plus three secondaries plus six tertiaries equals twelve slices of the color pizza.
art/art-color.90d985233587: Secondary colors. Mix two primaries: orange, green, violet. Red plus yellow equals orange; yellow plus blue equals green; blue plus red equals violet. Each secondary sits halfway between its two parents on the wheel. Secondary equals second step: two primaries holding hands.
art/art-color.57e59efd6da1: Primary colors. Colors you can’t mix from others — you mix everything else from them. Paint, RYB: red, yellow, blue. Light, RGB: red, green, blue — screens, stage lights. Printing, CMY and K: cyan, magenta, yellow and black. Paint equals RYB, Really Yummy Berries. Light equals RGB, Really Glowing Bulbs.
art/art-color.0fca42909644: Value: tints and shades. How light or dark a color is. Tint equals color and white, pink is a tint of red. Shade equals color and black, navy is a shade of blue. Value contrast is what makes a design readable from far away. Tint equals Touch of white. Shade equals Shadow, black.

art/art-history.1f49d966ca32: Street art and murals. Nineteen ninety, Berlin, Germany. Art leaves the museum. After the Berlin Wall fell, artists from around the world painted about one point three kilometers, zero point eight miles, of it — the East Side Gallery. Meanwhile in China: contemporary art was booming; Beijing’s seven nine eight Art District turned old factories into galleries in the early two thousands.
art/art-history.7f86474d4dce: Post-Impressionism. Eighteen eighty-nine, Saint-Rémy, France. Color and brushstroke show feeling, not just what the eye sees. Van Gogh’s sky swirls; Seurat built pictures from tiny dots, pointillism. Meanwhile in China: Ren Bonian and other Shanghai School painters mixed traditional ink painting with bright colors for city buyers.
art/art-history.36b3cf7ea471: Renaissance. about fifteen oh three to fifteen nineteen, Florence, Italy. Linear perspective and sfumato, “smoky”: no hard outlines, just soft glazes of oil paint so thin you can’t see brushstrokes. Meanwhile in China: the Ming dynasty — the Forbidden City was finished in fourteen twenty and Jingdezhen kilns were making blue-and-white porcelain.
art/art-history.3d9783c37813: Japanese woodblock prints. about eighteen thirty to eighteen thirty-two, Edo, Tokyo, Japan. Ukiyo-e prints: one carved wooden block per color, thousands of cheap copies. Hokusai used a new imported pigment — Prussian blue. Meanwhile in China: the Qing dynasty under the Daoguang Emperor; the Opium War would begin in eighteen forty.
art/art-history.6f75eeac9b8e: Song landscape painting. Eleven thirteen, Kaifeng, Northern Song China. Landscape becomes the hero. Eighteen-year-old Wang Ximeng painted mountains in brilliant mineral blue and green, azurite and malachite, on a scroll almost twelve meters, thirty-nine feet, long. Meanwhile in Europe: Romanesque churches with thick walls and round arches; the Bayeux Tapestry, about ten seventies, told a story in embroidery.
art/art-history.cd577fb9a73b: Impressionism. Eighteen seventy-two, Le Havre, France. Paint outdoors, fast, in broken dabs of color to catch changing light. Paint in metal tubes, invented eighteen forty-one, made it easy. A critic mocked this painting’s title — and the name “Impressionism” stuck. Meanwhile in China: the Self-Strengthening Movement, 洋务运动, was building China’s first modern factories and shipyards.
art/art-history.a4e73731e2bf: Cave art. about seventeen thousand years ago, Lascaux, France. Paint from the earth: red and yellow ochre, black charcoal — dabbed with moss or blown through hollow bones. Bumps in the rock became the bellies of animals. Meanwhile in China: people in Xianrendong Cave, Jiangxi, were making some of the world’s oldest known pottery, around twenty thousand years ago.
art/art-history.4addf86a97ef: Modern and abstract art. Nineteen thirty, Paris, Mondrian was Dutch. Art doesn’t have to show “things”: pure line, shape and color can be the whole subject, abstraction. Kandinsky had started painting abstracts around nineteen ten to nineteen thirteen. Meanwhile in China: Xu Beihong, 徐悲鸿, combined Western drawing with Chinese ink — famous for his galloping horses.
art/art-history.55549acb654b: Ancient Egypt. about thirteen fifty B C E, Thebes, Egypt. Rules beat realism: head and legs in profile, but eye and shoulders from the front. Important people are drawn bigger, hierarchical scale. Meanwhile in China: the Shang dynasty, about sixteen hundred to ten forty-six B C E, cast giant bronze vessels and carved writing on oracle bones.
art/art-history.02612d17eb87: Ancient Greece. Four hundred forty-seven to four hundred thirty-two B C E, Athens, Greece. Beauty equals harmony and math: ideal proportions, balanced columns, statues standing in a relaxed, natural pose. Meanwhile in China: the late Spring and Autumn or early Warring States period — Confucius, five hundred fifty-one to four hundred seventy-nine B C E, had died a few decades earlier.

art/art-chinese.9df2bbd6c552: Four Treasures of the Study. Brush, ink, paper and inkstone — 笔, 墨, 纸, 砚. Brushes are made of animal hair, goat, weasel, rabbit, set in bamboo. Ink sticks of soot and glue are ground with water on a stone inkstone. Xuan paper, 宣纸, from Anhui soaks up ink instantly — no erasing! 笔墨纸砚: Brush, Ink, Paper, Stone.

art/art-sculpture.fa23504bf1ff: A turn through the torso and a forward knee give this standing figure movement. The three D view is a scan of a museum plaster cast of the marble. Compare the bare torso with the folds twisting below it.

art/art-theater.5765850f5f3d: Kunqu developed around Kunshan and influenced many other forms, earning the nickname “ancestor of a hundred operas.” UNESCO proclaimed it a Masterpiece in two thousand one and inscribed it on its Representative List in two thousand eight. In The Peony Pavilion, listen to how the voice and flute move together.
art/art-theater.104853f2715b: New York’s Chinatown has a tradition of staging opera in Cantonese. Yuèqǔ is Cantonese narrative singing, and some of its songs come from opera. UNESCO inscribed Cantonese opera on its Representative List in two thousand nine. Listen to the two performers sing to each other.

art/art-architecture.2cb0fc4e6ba4: This plaster cast is in Gallery three of the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge, England. The original relief came from the fifth-century B C E Parthenon. Rotate the cast sideways and see how far the figures stand out.
art/art-architecture.428f47d7e10b: The curves of a pointed arch meet at a peak. Tall stained-glass windows color daylight and draw your eyes up. In “The Blue Virgin,” the light-blue central panels date to the twelfth century. The surrounding glass is from the thirteenth century.
art/art-architecture.a51703ef5907: Eight columns line each short end, and seventeen line each long side, counting the corner columns on both sides. The platform at the columns is about sixty-nine point five meters long and thirty point nine meters wide. The long side is about two point two five times the short side.
